thread:
alex: heads up — incoming support ticket #2345. Customer in us-east-1 reporting p99 ~300-800ms for simple completions. They say the SDK is set to use us-east endpoints but traces show responses from eu-central-1. attaching clipped logs below.

alex: log sample: 
[2025-11-04T12:01:05Z] client.request id=abc123 endpoint=https://api.redwood.example.com/us-east-1 path=/v1/completions latency=312ms -> response.headers.x-serving-region=eu-central-1 x-fallback-reason=capacity
[2025-11-04T12:01:07Z] client.request id=def456 endpoint=https://api.redwood.example.com/us-east-1 path=/v1/completions latency=721ms -> response.headers.x-serving-region=eu-central-1 x-routed-via=router-3a

alex: customer uses SDK v2.4.1 with hedgedRequests=true, retryPolicy: {minBackoffMs:50,maxBackoffMs:400,attempts:3}, preferLocalRegion=true

priya: thanks — can you paste repro steps they ran? also do we have a request id from our edge logs to correlate?

alex: they repro with a simple loop: 
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 5); do
  curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "X-Region: us-east-1" \
    "https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/completions" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":5}'
done
```
Responses show 200 but headers: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Serving-Region: eu-central-1
X-Fallback-Reason: capacity
X-Request-Id: abc123
```

josh: rough theory: SDK's hedgedRequests fires parallel attempts to primary + fallback region to reduce tail latency. if the primary edge signals capacity, the router may route the active connection to a fallback region. with hedged + short timeouts + our smart-routing fallback, clients can end up hitting eu region even when origin header requests us-east.

josh: can you confirm if the client is using hedged *per request* (parallel) vs hedged with fast-cancel? hedged without cancel will produce cross-region double traffic.

alex: they have hedgedRequests=true and no fast-cancel (v2.4.1 default).

priya: ok — two things to triage: 1) confirm router fallback metrics around the timestamps (capacity tripping?) 2) check DNS / load-balancer TTL and whether we returned eu endpoints to that client recently. Also check if the SDK is resolving a region-specific endpoint to an IP belonging to eu.

infra-bot: notice: rollout smart-routing-v2 staged 2025-11-04T11:58:00Z to region us-east-1 routers; change: improved fallback granularity.

josh: that rollout could explain it — new fallback logic tries cross-region fallback faster. If hedgedRequests is enabled we might see more cross-region hits.

alex: repro plan I'm running locally: set SDK hedgedRequests=false, timeout=1200ms and run the curl loop. will also capture packet traces and note resolved IP.

priya: please also run: 
```bash
nslookup api.redwood.example.com us-east-1-dns
curl -I https://<resolved-ip>/v1/healthz
```
We want to see if the resolved A record maps to eu IPs intermittently.

alex: quick findings: DNS resolved to 52.34.12.9 then 18.194.22.7 in same run. reverse lookup shows 18.194.22.7 in eu-central. TTL low (30s).

josh: low TTL + hedgedRequests is a smoking gun. When TTL flips between region IPs and hedged fires, you can end up with request attempts landing in different regions. Combine with fast fallback, client observes correct endpoint but server returns eu serving region.

tina: notes — action items: 1) eng-runtime to throttle cross-region fallbacks when hedgedRequests header present or when resolved IP set shows mixed-region; 2) support to ask customer to upgrade SDK or disable hedgedRequests as short-term mitigation; 3) infra to inspect smart-routing rollout metrics and rollback if errors spike. assigning. :spiral_notepad: 

alex: I've advised the customer to disable hedgedRequests and increase client backoff. They reported immediate p95 improvement (from ~500ms to ~80ms).

priya: can eng-runtime add a defensive header check: if client includes X-Preferred-Region and the resolved IP belongs to another region, prefer sticking to the resolved IP until TTL expires? Or at least log a routed-region-mismatch metric.

josh: agree — logging metric is low-risk and will speed debugging. we should also consider SDK change: hedgedRequests should include fast-cancel by default and a flag to avoid cross-region hedging.

tina: filing ENG-789 to track work: add mismatch logging, SDK recommendation, and evaluate smart-routing rollback. I'll drop notes into the ticket and loop eng-runtime on it.

alex: thanks — saving traces and will attach to ENG-789. ping me for any follow-ups. :thumbsup:
